title: TypeScript SDK: backpressure-handshake adapter between async iterator and Web Streams
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Consumers of the TypeScript SDK use both async iterators (for Node/Deno idioms) and Web Streams (for browser/edge runtimes). Current adapter layers are functional but show inconsistent backpressure semantics across environments: consumers cannot reliably pause/resume, cancellation sometimes leaves the server-side KV cache hot, and resumable reads are brittle when the underlying fetch stream reconnects.

Goal: Implement a small, explicit 'handshake' protocol in the SDK's adapter layer that preserves backpressure semantics bi-directionally between async iterators and ReadableStream consumers. The adapter should: 1) provide an explicit "pause/resume/ack" signal path so consumers can request the server to hold or release tokens, 2) propagate cancellation and finalization in a single canonical sequence so downstream can checkpoint and reuse KV cache entries, and 3) behave identically on Node, Deno, and browsers (polyfills allowed but behavior must be consistent).

Why unique: Instead of ad-hoc buffering or relying on engine scheduling, this ticket standardizes a lightweight protocol (handshake frames) layered on top of the existing framing codec that can be implemented in the SDK without server changes. It focuses on ergonomics (small API surface for app authors), deterministic semantics for tests, and minimal runtime overhead.

Trade-offs considered: Using a full protocol layer (e.g., control frames over the network) was rejected because it requires server changes and deployment coordination. Relying solely on existing ReadableStream backpressure is unreliable in certain Node versions and when streams are transformed; adding handshake introduces slight complexity but gives deterministic semantics.

Acceptance criteria below spell out behavioral guarantees and examples for migration.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter exposes a small opt-in API: adapter.handshake() returns an object with pause(), resume(), ack() hooks usable by both async iterator and ReadableStream consumers.
Pausing an async iterator causes the corresponding remote prefix K/V caching to be held (simulated in unit tests) until resume() or ack() is called.
Cancellation from either side triggers a canonical finalization sequence: send finalize signal -> await ack -> release resources. No leaked pending promises after finalize in unit/integration tests.
Behavior tests pass identically on Node 18+, Deno latest, and Chromium-based browsers (CI using Playwright).
Migration guide and examples (3 short snippets) added to docs/ts/streaming.md and linked from the SDK README.
E2E smoke PR created that demonstrates adapter in sample app with dual consumers (for-await-of and ReadableStream pipeTo) and shows no data duplication/ordering regressions.
Performance overhead measured: handshake adds <3% CPU in typical low-latency workloads and does not increase median token latency by more than 5ms in dominated cases.
implementation_notes:
High-level plan: (1) implement a small HandshakeChannel class inside packages/sdk/streaming/adapters/ that multiplexes control frames with existing framing codec; (2) expose a Typescript-friendly wrapper that yields an async iterator while exposing a .stream() method returning a ReadableStream for browser usage; (3) add adapters for existing consumer helpers (forEachToken, text() consumer) to opt into handshake via an option flag; (4) implement deterministic tests using fake transport (no network) to simulate server-side KV cache behavior and verify finalization semantics.

API sketch: const { iterator, stream, control } = createHandshakeAdapter(fetchResponse, { enableHandshake: true }); for await (const tok of iterator) { if (control.shouldPause()) await control.pauseUntil(ok); } // or in browser: const rs = stream(); rs.getReader().read()... control.ack()

Care: polyfills for ReadableStream in older Node used only in test harness; avoid shipping polyfills to customers by runtime-detecting environment. Keep public API minimal to reduce cognitive load for users.
tests: Unit: deterministic fake transport that asserts order of control frames during pause/resume/cancel.
Integration: sample app (packages/examples/dual-consumer) with Playwright test that mounts the browser-based stream and Node consumer simultaneously and verifies no token duplication.
Stress: concurrency test that opens 200 adapters, random pause/resume, verify no memory growth beyond expected and all resources finalized.
Perf: microbench harness measuring CPU and median latency with handshake enabled vs disabled for 10k tokens.
Backward compat: ensure consumers not opting into handshake behave exactly as before.
updates: 2025-02-18 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket and wrote initial proposal, included API sketch and rationale.
2025-02-21 Miguel Ortega: Spike complete — prototype HandshakeChannel implemented in a local branch, basic pause/resume semantics verified in node unit tests.
2025-02-25 Design review (Lina Roberts): requested simpler public surface; suggested: expose only control.pauseUntil(predicate) and control.finalize(). Will incorporate.
2025-02-28 Engineering review: noted edge-case where stream.transform() can swallow backpressure; added tests that pipe through TransformStream to validate semantics.
2025-03-02 PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1624 — includes implementation, unit tests, and a sample example. Requesting SDK team review.

2025-03-04 QA: found a flaky case in Playwright where reader.releaseLock() timing caused duplicate ack; mitigation added by introducing a 10ms debounce before sending ack on browser path. TODO: evaluate if debounce required long-term.
next_steps: Address Playwright flake (debounce long-term fix or alternate handshake ACK strategy), finalize docs and examples, coordinate with release manager to include in sdk-2025.04. If QA is green, merge PR and cut a preview release for integration teams.
notes_for_release_notes: TypeScript SDK: introduced optional backpressure-handshake adapter for deterministic pause/resume/cancellation semantics between async iterators and Web Streams. Opt-in via createHandshakeAdapter(..., { enableHandshake: true }). Improves reliability for dual-consumer scenarios and reduces KV cache leaks on cancellation.
